answer: Each identity links to a blog with a long tenure: posts published steadily for years, with comments, links, and an archive anyone can read. A dune moves with the wind, but a blog with five years of posts does not: it stands as a public record of a real person thinking in public. A haven for a farm's blogs is nowhere to be found: their posts are all generated in one week, all on the same topics, all linking to each other. The vine of a real blog grows slowly, post by post, and the network trusts the growth it can see.
